properties.name: MEASURED AND LANDED — capping glibc arenas halves resident memory (424 -> 199 MB) for no measurable write throughput cost, and the first two rounds would have supported either answer
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-13, two servers on identical copies of reflow2's own 4,403-node store, same release binary, same box. Taken because req:one-open-design-costs-a-deliberate-amount-of-memory requires that the throughput traded away be measured ALONGSIDE the memory saved — the root-cause finding had measured only memory, so the fix could not honestly land on it.

    resident memory     424 MB -> 199 MB   (-53%, identical in every round)
    write throughput     7.7/s ->  7.8/s   (+0.6%, interleaved median)
    export latency       0.81s ->  0.73s   (-9%, single round, not repeated)

🛑 THE FIRST TWO ROUNDS WOULD HAVE JUSTIFIED EITHER CONCLUSION, and this is the part worth keeping:

    round 1 (sequential)    write throughput  -0.9%   -> "the trade is free, ship it"
    round 2 (sequential)    write throughput -30.1%   -> "this costs a third of write speed"

The control ITSELF moved 14.5/s -> 10.7/s between those rounds — a 26% drift with nothing changed — so neither number measured the allocator. Had only round 1 been taken, a fix would have landed on a claim a repeat contradicted within the minute.

⭐ WHAT RESOLVED IT: interleaving. Alternating A/B/A/B in batches of 40 cancels monotonic drift, and the medians came back 7.7 against 7.8. The decisive evidence is not the medians but the SPREAD — 7.4-14.7 for the default arm and 7.3-14.5 for the capped one, both bimodal, nearly identical. Two arms with the same variance profile are being moved by the same thing, and it is not the arena count.

WHAT LANDED:
 · crates/reflow2-mcp/src/shared.rs — a spawned --serve-shared daemon inherits MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2. It must be set by the PARENT: glibc reads it at the first allocation, before main runs, so a process cannot choose its own arena count.
 · Dockerfile — the same, as ENV, for the published image.
 · An explicit setting in the launcher's environment WINS and is never overruled: whoever started reflow2 may have a thread-bound workload that wants the arenas.

VERIFIED END TO END, not only in the unit test: a daemon spawned through `--shared` was found via its rendezvous file and `/proc/<pid>/environ` read back `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`. The two unit tests pin the DECISION (cap by default, never overrule an explicit setting) and deliberately do not read /proc, because that would make the check Linux-only and this repo runs on macOS too.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED:
 · No CI test asserts the memory number. A resident-memory assertion would be exactly the kind of environment-dependent gate that goes intermittently red — this session found one such race the same day — so it is deliberately absent rather than forgotten.
 · Export latency was measured once and not repeated; the -9% should not be quoted as a result.
 · Only glibc. musl's allocator is different and the image's base libc was not re-checked after this change.
 · This does not touch the unexplained residue: two LIVE agent sessions sit above the band that five controlled arms cannot leave, and duration/session churn remains the one unvaried candidate.
